page: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a large 50 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 262 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the E16-4s_v3 exhibits a clear tradeoff between massive memory capacity and processing throughput. CPU-centric metrics, such as stress-ng single-core (1244.28) and multi-core (3272.27) performance, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench scores (976.0 single-core and 2196.0 multi-core) and Passmark CPU scores (3961.34) are categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance for large block reads (23.14 GB/sec) and writes (16.82 GB/sec), though the Passmark memory score of 2279.8 reaches average levels. Application-level benchmarks, including Redis SET operations at 3.11 million operations per second and static web serving at 3.24 GB/sec, also align with the bottom 25% performance tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-4s_v3 offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring large memory allocations without demanding high CPU performance. This resource distribution is appropriate for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads such as caching layers, small to medium relational databases with large working sets, and basic data buffering. However, it is less effective for compute-heavy tasks, high-throughput web serving, or complex parallel processing due to the constrained CPU capabilities and weak multi-threaded decompression performance.
